rationale: X gives a detailed and mostly source-grounded strategy, but it is not at parity because it gets the normal load-hook timing wrong. Booting a generated application does not itself load `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest`; after `rails/test_help`, that hook is normally still pending until an integration test class first references the constant. Therefore a post-require mutation of `ActiveSupport::TestCase.fixture_paths` made before that first reference is included when IntegrationTest later executes `+=`, contrary to X's proposed assertion that IntegrationTest must not see it. This materially mis-specifies the requested inheritance, before/after-require, and application-extra-path contract.

shortcomings.summary: It incorrectly assumes the IntegrationTest hook always runs immediately during `rails/test_help`.
shortcomings.evidence: X says the application boot has already loaded `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest` and that all hooks therefore run immediately. A fresh checkout probe showed that after application boot and `require "rails/test_help"`, only `:active_support_test_case` had a loaded base; `:action_dispatch_integration_test` and `:action_controller_test_case` remained empty until their constants were referenced.

shortcomings.summary: Its post-require extra-path black-box expectation is false in the normal generated-helper sequence.
shortcomings.evidence: Case 3 says appending to `ActiveSupport::TestCase.fixture_paths` after the require must not affect IntegrationTest because it has already snapshotted the array. In a direct probe, appending `/tmp/extra` after `rails/test_help` and only then defining an `ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest` subclass caused the deferred hook to copy the updated parent list, and IntegrationTest contained `/tmp/extra`; the proposed negative test would fail against current Rails.

shortcomings.summary: The strategy was not dynamically checked despite hinging on require and lazy-load timing.
shortcomings.evidence: X's transcript performs extensive source reads but runs no focused test or minimal hook-state probe. The central mistake is exactly the kind of temporal behavior that a one-process check of `ActiveSupport`'s loaded-hook table or a generated-app integration subclass would have exposed.

strengths.summary: It accurately inventories most require-time effects and path-shape details.
strengths.evidence: X correctly covers the production abort, schema maintenance, Active Record branch, included fixture/query modules, absolute string paths and trailing-slash distinctions, engine fixture hooks, TestCase `.uniq`, IntegrationTest `+=` duplication, file fixtures without Active Record, and dynamic route lookup in `before_setup`.

strengths.summary: It proposes broad observable coverage rather than relying only on class attributes.
strengths.evidence: The matrix exercises real YAML fixture access, `file_fixture`, file upload, query assertions, integration requests, missing directories, exact and representational duplicates, pre/post-require classes, repeated require/load, engine paths, skip-Active-Record behavior, production abort, and two application boots.

strengths.summary: Its isolation and existing-suite guidance is practical and well scoped.
strengths.evidence: X recommends generated-app tests under `ActiveSupport::Testing::Isolation`, `build_app`/`teardown_app`, disabled parallel workers, no parent-process `rails/test_help` require, and focused railties, Active Record, and Active Support test files. It also correctly warns about global load hooks, `$LOADED_FEATURES`, class attributes, autorun, and fixture caches.
